title: 19th Sitting of second session of 2026
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla; Deputy Speaker Ahmed Saleem took the chair after the 10:28-11:04 break
summary: The sitting opened at 09:02 with the Speaker welcoming youth visitors from the Practice Parliament programme. Most of the morning was question time with the Minister of Islamic Affairs and Endowments, where members asked when mosques and Islamic centres in their islands would be built or opened, and about Hajj quotas and the zakat fund. After a break, the preliminary debate began on Dr. Ahmed Shamheed's resolution urging the government to stop the Maldives Pal Residence Programme and disclose its agreements; the proposer and two members spoke before this part ends, with no vote yet. This part covers the second half of the debate on Dr. Ahmed Shamheed's resolution asking the government to halt the 'Maldives Palm Residence Programme' (permanent residence in return for investment) and disclose its agreements. Government-aligned members opposed the resolution, saying residence-for-investment schemes already exist and bring in money, while Kendhoo's Mauroof Zakir argued that a full law should be passed before the programme goes ahead. The Majlis then moved to the government's bill on leasing uninhabited islands and lagoons, where speakers supporting it spoke of decentralisation and wider access to leases, and opposition members raised concerns about presidential powers and unclear criteria. The debate on both items was not finished when time ran out, and the sitting closed until 5 August 2026.

items.outcome: Minister answered; 15 follow-up questions on mosque projects, Hulhumale' mosques, Hajj quota and funding

speakers.name: Dr. Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed
positions: Said Fenaka took over the Kudarikilu mosque, with work expected to start 15 August 2026 and about a year allowed.
Said many mosque projects began before the 2023 election without budgets, and more mosques should open before Ramadan.
Said the Hulhumale' grand mosque is Saudi-funded with works aimed for September, and Hajj quota growth depends on Saudi ties.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked when work on the Kudarikilu mosque would start and finish, and whether Fenaka has mosque-building experience and funds.
Asked about the slow Kamadhoo mosque, invited the minister to visit Kendhoo, and raised a suspected grave at a Thulhaadhoo mosque.
Asked what is being done for Quran teaching in Kendhoo's islands.
On the resolution, argued the public has a right to know the programme's terms and that a law should be passed before it goes ahead; questioned spending on the Fushidhiggaru reef reclamation.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked when work starts on the Fuvahmulah Islamic centre and whether mosque staff could move under ministry management.
Asked how far the 79-project programme and the Hulhumale' grand mosque have progressed.
Asked how the ministry is seeking more Islamic grants, linked to OIC membership and the Palestine issue.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Opposed the resolution, citing the 2015 corporate residence scheme and saying the programme would bring investment and benefit the economy.
Raised two points of order objecting that remarks on the programme and on the bill were off topic or misleading.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Asked for the latest on the planned Hoarafushi Islamic centre and the opening date of the Thurakunu mosque.
Said the Thurakunu mosque is nearly finished and asked when it will open.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Asked when the planned mosque at Feevak will start and finish.
Supported the leasing bill as a step in decentralisation that lets councils earn income and creates a fairer lease system.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Asked whether the Waqf programme could bring an Islamic or Quran centre to Addu City's Feydhoo, and whether new mosques will include ablution houses.
Opposed the resolution, saying the country is not being sold and that residence visas for investors have existed since 2015.
Said investors' deposits in Maldivian banks and long-term resort leases benefit the economy.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Asked the minister to explain how wide the ministry's mandate is, since members and young preachers raise it often.
Supported the leasing bill, saying it replaces the existing law with a stricter system and opens island leases to smaller and mid-sized businesses.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked whether the mosque materials at Nellaidhoo could be redesigned and a damaged minaret at Kurinbi fixed quickly.
Asked whether the long Hajj queue can be shortened given the Saudi relationship.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Asked whether the minister plans an Islamic centre in Kudahuvadhoo, noting the council has applied.
Supported the leasing bill, saying leases should reach middle-class businesses and not only the highest bidder, and raised concern about reef reclamation.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Introduced a resolution urging a halt to the Maldives Pal Residence Programme, disclosure of its agreements, and a residency law passed by the Majlis.
Argued it runs without a Majlis law, with terms undisclosed, and raises sovereignty and tax concerns.
Raised concerns about the leasing bill: who decides an island's use, the powers given to the president and councils, missing criteria for agriculture or tourism islands, and foreign-only enclaves.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Said burials in Male' area are costly and a big challenge, and asked whether the ministry has a different system in mind.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Asked how long the Hanimaadhoo mosque, under construction for years, will take, comparing it to the Hulhumale' to Vilimale' bridge.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Asked how many mosques finished since this government took office and how many are now being built or in use.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked when work starts on the mosque foundation laid at Noomaara.
Asked whether zakat fund aid could prioritise low-income applicants, citing easier access to other schemes.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked when the promised extra mosque at Rasdhoo starts, and what has been done about Umrah groups that took money and did not deliver.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Said the Kulhudhuffushi waqf building is progressing fast but the Islamic centre redesign is slow, and asked how much space it will provide.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Thanked the government for more Hajj quota for poorer citizens and asked for further detail.

speakers.name: Abdulla Sodig
positions: Asked when the stalled Hithadhoo Islamic centre and mosque, begun in 2023, will be finished and opened.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shameez
positions: Asked when the Madaveli mosque promised by the President will start, and about the Nadella mosque, ablution houses and contractors.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Thanked the minister and said he understands the Faresmaathodaa mosque is stuck at tender stage.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Asked what policies are meant to raise attendance at mosques, and about crowding at Huraa mosque on holidays.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Thanked the government for the Vashafaru mosque and asked when work will start on the Filladhoo and Kela mosques.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Praised the Dhiddhoo Islamic centre and asked the ministry to speed up staffing and furniture.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Asked for the current status of the Masjid Izzudheen Male' rebuilding.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Asked when the long-unfinished Kondey mosque will be completed, and whether budgets cover the dollar rate rise.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Asked when the delayed SJ Construction mosque in Hulhumale' North will be done, and about the leaking Phase 1 mosque.

speakers.name: Ali Ashrag
positions: Asked when the Hirilandhoo mosque will be completed, and added a remark about MDP members' questions.

speakers.name: Ahmed Thariq
positions: Said the resolution is contradictory and premature because a residency law is being drafted for the Majlis.
Argued such residency schemes are common abroad and can bring investment.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Said the programme is still at consultancy stage and any law will come to the Majlis.
Argued residency schemes broaden the tax base beyond tourism and add fees and jobs.

decisions: Agenda for the 4 August 2026 sitting was announced by the chair.
The chair set the debate time on the residency resolution at 4 hours, split by party (PNC 2h33m, MDP 35m, MDA 14m, JP 12m, MNP 12m, 7 minutes each for others).
The sitting took a break from 10:28 to 11:04 and resumed under the Deputy Speaker.
Debate time for the Palm Residence resolution (item 6.1) ended with the debate unfinished.
The chair moved on to agenda item 7 and continued debate on the island leasing bill (7.1), with time split by party.
The sitting was closed; the next sitting is set for Wednesday 5 August 2026 at 9:00.
